inconsistencies: Chain: #36091 (debug output for tested types) is a stated prerequisite for #35713 (remove Boost as unit test runner); review #36091 first, and #35713 should not be merged in a way that strands it.

Overlap: #35139 (new ASSERT macros) and #35713 (in-tree runner with its own assertion decomposition) both replace Boost.Test assertion machinery. A single approach decision should be made; #35713 is the broader one and should set the direction.

Overlap: #32554 (generate blocks at runtime) and #36254 (add static undo data for block413567) are competing answers to the same stale-benchmark-fixture problem; #32554 also supersedes #32457. Decide the fixture strategy before merging either; #36254 is the smaller immediate correctness fix.
#36371 is stacked on #36369 (not in this category list) — the base must land first.
#35442 depends on #35433 (RBF argument deprecation) and currently bundles its commits; it cannot be judged independently of that.
#36427 is a backport of already-merged #36404 to 32.x; it duplicates master work by design and its value is confined to the maintenance branch.

#36074 and #36087 both reshape assertion includes/conventions across test files and will conflict with each other and with #35139/#35713; sequence them after the runner decision to avoid repeated scripted-diff churn.
#35994's author has stated a preference for abandoning the PR in favour of a manual rewrite — intent should be confirmed before any reviewer time is spent.
result.notes: No P1 assigned: nothing here is a current CI-breaking or fund/consensus-safety failure that would be seriously harmful to leave another cycle; the strongest items are recurring-flakiness fixes and high-risk-path coverage, which sit naturally at P2. The P2 head of the list follows the category's stated order (flaky/misleading-test signal, then consensus/p2p coverage, then framework capability), and the long P3 tail is ordered speed-and-signal first, additive coverage next, developer-workflow tooling last.
